answer: The cedar graph is validated at intake and the ember frontier is published, thus the ancestry of every answer is public, and nebula anchors the chain at a checkpoint. A freshly minted alias has no ancestry, so it must first attach itself to real accepted work: 215 new identities mean that many orphan roots to graft by hand rather than print, and each root still needs its own identity record. Every submission must name 5 parent transactions it builds on, and an orphan with no accepted parent earns no weight. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
